description: Inheriting something small and useless and wanting it. It is usually small and it is usually not announced as important by anyone present.
energy_note: Nobody says at the time that this is the good bit.

description: Family goods are almost never spontaneous. They rest on years of somebody turning up, which is invisible until the day it pays.
energy_note: Years of ordinary attendance, cashing in at once.

description: Asked years later what made it good, people name the company rather than the content. The Harvard Study of Adult Development has been producing that result for eighty-seven years.
notes: Harvard Study of Adult Development: relationship quality is the strongest single predictor of health and happiness.

description: A functioning health system, or a document, or money - which is where the other half of this game attaches.
energy_note: The requirement is usually that everybody can be reached.
notes: Pairs with FAM, IDR and STA categories in assets/text/{palestine,iran,nigeria}.

description: It stops being an event and becomes a reference point - retold, compared against, and eventually shorthand inside one family for a whole kind of day.
energy_note: It turns into the story about it.
notes: Experiential purchases retain value through memory where material ones decay; people are markedly unwilling to trade the memory away.
